units.Daniel 2:24: Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to kill all Babylonia’s learned men, and said, “Do not destroy Babylonia’s learned men. Bring me to the king, and I will disclose every detail to him.”
units.Daniel 2:25: Then Arioch urgently brought Daniel to the king and said, “I have found a wise man from the captivity of the sons of Judea who will disclose every detail to the king.”
units.Daniel 2:26: The king answered Daniel, who was called Baltasar in Chaldean, “Will you be able to disclose to me the vision I saw and its interpretation?”
units.Daniel 2:27: Daniel spoke aloud before the king, “Disclosure of the mystery the king saw does not belong to wise men, sorcerers, incantation-singers, or gazarenes,
units.Daniel 2:28: but there is a God in heaven who uncovers mysteries, who has disclosed to King Nebuchadnezzar what must happen in the last days. O king, live for ever! This is the dream and the vision of your head upon your bed:
units.Daniel 2:29: You, O king, reclining upon your bed, saw everything that must happen in the last days, and the Revealer of mysteries disclosed to you what must happen.
units.Daniel 2:30: This mystery was revealed to me because of no wisdom in me beyond all people; rather, so that it might be disclosed to the king, what you conceived in your heart was made known to me.
units.Daniel 2:31: You, O king, saw a single image. That image was exceedingly large, its appearance was extraordinary as it stood before you, and the image’s appearance was frightening.
units.Daniel 2:32: Its head was good gold, its chest and arms silver, and its belly and thighs bronze,
units.Daniel 2:33: its legs iron, and its feet partly iron and partly earthenware.
units.Daniel 2:34: You watched until a stone was cut from a mountain without hands. It struck the image on its feet of iron and earthenware and ground them down.
units.Daniel 2:35: Then the iron, earthenware, bronze, silver, and gold were ground fine together, becoming finer than chaff on a threshing floor. The wind scattered them so that nothing remained of them. The stone that struck the image became a great mountain and struck the whole earth.
units.Daniel 2:36: This was the vision; now we will state its interpretation before the king.
units.Daniel 2:37: You, O king, are king of kings, and the Lord of heaven has given you rule, kingdom, strength, honor, and glory.
units.Daniel 2:38: Throughout the inhabited world He has handed over into your hands human beings, wild beasts, birds of heaven, and fish of the sea, to rule them all. You are the golden head.
units.Daniel 2:39: After you a kingdom lesser than you will arise, and another, a third kingdom of bronze, which will rule the whole earth.
units.Daniel 2:40: A fourth kingdom will be strong like iron that subdues everything and cuts down every tree, and the whole earth will be shaken.
units.Daniel 2:41: As you saw its feet partly potter’s earthenware and partly iron, another kingdom, divided in two, will be within it, just as you saw iron mixed with clay earthenware.
units.Daniel 2:42: The toes of the feet were partly iron and partly earthenware; part of the kingdom will be strong and part shattered.
units.Daniel 2:43: As you saw iron mixed with clay earthenware, they will be mingled in human generation, but will neither agree nor have goodwill toward one another, just as iron cannot blend with earthenware.
units.Daniel 2:44: In the times of these kings the God of heaven will establish another kingdom, which will exist for ever and will not be destroyed. This kingdom will not leave another nation; it will strike and obliterate these kingdoms and will itself stand for ever,
units.Daniel 2:45: just as you saw a stone cut from a mountain without hands, pounding together the earthenware, iron, bronze, silver, and gold. The great God has shown the king what will happen in the last days. The vision is exact, and its interpretation trustworthy.”
units.Daniel 2:46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell face down on the ground and prostrated himself before Daniel. He ordered sacrifices and libations made to him.
units.Daniel 2:47: The king spoke aloud to Daniel, “Truly your God is God of gods and Lord of kings, the One who alone brings hidden mysteries to light, because you have been able to disclose this mystery.”
units.Daniel 2:48: Then King Nebuchadnezzar exalted Daniel, gave him many great gifts, placed him over Babylonia’s affairs, and appointed him ruler and leader of all Babylonia’s learned men.
units.Daniel 2:49: Daniel petitioned the king that Sedrach, Misach, and Abdenago be appointed over Babylonia’s affairs. Daniel remained in the royal court.
units.Daniel 4:25: They will lead you away into custody and send you to a deserted place.
units.Daniel 4:26: The root of the tree that was left, since it was not uprooted, means that the place of your throne will be preserved for you for a time and an hour. Behold! They are preparing against you; they will scourge you and bring the judgments upon you.
units.Daniel 4:27: The Lord lives in heaven, and His authority is over all the earth. Entreat Him concerning your sins, and redeem all your injustices by almsgiving, so that gentleness may be granted you, you may have many days upon your royal throne, and He may not destroy you. Love these words, for my word is accurate and your time is full.’”
units.Daniel 4:28: At the completion of the words, Nebuchadnezzar, when he heard the judgment of the vision, kept the words in his heart.
units.Daniel 4:29: After twelve months, the king was walking upon the city walls with all his glory and passing over its towers.
units.Daniel 4:30: He spoke and said, “This is great Babylon, which I built, and it will be called the house of my kingship through the strength of my might, for the honor of my glory.”
units.Daniel 4:31: At the completion of his word, he heard a voice from heaven: “To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: Babylon’s kingdom has been taken from you and is given to another, a despised man in your house. Behold! I appoint him over your kingdom; he will take your authority, glory, and luxury, so that you may recognize that the God of heaven has authority over human kingship and will give it to whomever He wishes. By sunrise another king will rejoice in your house and take possession of your glory, strength, and authority.
units.Daniel 4:32: The angels will pursue you for seven years. You will neither be seen nor speak with any human being. They will feed you grass like an ox, and your pasture will be the earth’s greenery. Behold! In place of your glory they will bind you, and another will have your luxurious house and your kingdom.
units.Daniel 4:33: By morning everything will be fulfilled upon you, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon; nothing of all this will fail.”
units.Daniel 4:33a: “I, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, was bound for seven years. They fed me grass like an ox, and I ate the earth’s greenery. After seven years I devoted my soul to supplication and pleaded concerning my sins before the Lord, the God of heaven; concerning my acts of ignorance I entreated the great God of gods.
units.Daniel 4:33b: My hair became like an eagle’s wings, and my nails like a lion’s. My flesh and my heart were changed; I walked naked with the wild animals of the earth. I saw a dream, and apprehensions seized me. After a time a deep sleep took hold of me, and drowsiness fell upon me.
units.Daniel 4:34: At the completion of the seven years, the time of my release came. My sins and my acts of ignorance reached their full measure before the God of heaven. I entreated the great God of gods concerning my acts of ignorance, and an angel called to me from heaven, saying, ‘Nebuchadnezzar, serve the holy God of heaven and give glory to the Most High; the kingship of your nation is restored to you.’
units.Daniel 4:36: At that time my kingdom was restored to me and my glory returned to me.
units.Daniel 4:37: I give thanks to the Most High and praise Him who created heaven and earth, seas and rivers, and everything in them. I give thanks and praise, for He is God of gods, Lord of lords, and King of kings. He performs signs and wonders and changes seasons and times, taking kingdoms from kings and appointing others in their place.
units.Daniel 4:37a: From now on I will worship Him. Trembling has seized me through fear of Him, and I praise all His holy ones. For the gods of the nations have no strength in themselves to transfer one king’s kingdom to another king, to kill and make alive, to perform signs and great and fearsome wonders, or to change exceedingly great affairs, as the God of heaven has done in me, changing great affairs concerning me. Throughout all the days of my reign I will offer sacrifices to the Most High on behalf of my soul, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. I will do what is acceptable before Him—I and my people, my nation and my countries under my authority. Whoever has spoken against the God of heaven, and whoever is caught speaking anything against Him, I will condemn to death.”
units.Daniel 4:37b: King Nebuchadnezzar wrote a circular letter to all the nations in every place, to the countries and all languages dwelling in every country, from generation to generation: “Praise the Lord, the God of heaven, and gloriously bring Him sacrifice and offering. I, king of kings, gloriously give thanks to Him, because He has dealt with me in this way: on that very day He seated me upon my throne; I regained my authority and my kingdom among my people, and my greatness was restored to me.”
units.Daniel 4:37c: “King Nebuchadnezzar to all nations, all countries, and all who dwell in them: May peace be multiplied to you at every time. Now I will explain to you the deeds that the great God has done with me. It pleased me to demonstrate to you and to your learned experts that there is a God, and His wonders are great; His kingship is an everlasting kingship, His authority from generation to generation.” He sent letters concerning everything that had happened to him in his kingdom to all the nations under his kingship.
units.Matthew 24:1: Jesus went out from the temple and was going away, when His disciples came to show Him the temple buildings.
units.Matthew 24:2: He answered them, “Do you not see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone will be left here upon another that will not be thrown down.”
units.Matthew 24:3: As He sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things happen, and what is the sign of Thy coming and the consummation of the age?”
units.Matthew 24:15: So when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of through Daniel the prophet standing in a holy place—let the reader understand—
units.Matthew 24:16: then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
units.Matthew 24:17: Let the one on the housetop not go down to take things from his house,
units.Matthew 24:18: and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
units.Matthew 24:19: Woe to those with child and those nursing infants in those days!
units.Matthew 24:20: Pray that your flight may not occur in winter or on a Sabbath.
units.Matthew 24:21: For then there will be great affliction such as has not happened from the beginning of the world until now, and certainly will never happen again.
units.Matthew 24:22: If those days had not been shortened, no flesh would have been saved; but because of the chosen, those days will be shortened.
units.Matthew 24:23: Then if anyone tells you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ!’ or ‘Here!’ do not believe it.
units.Matthew 24:24: For false christs and false prophets will arise and give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
units.Matthew 24:25: Behold, I have told you beforehand.
units.Matthew 24:26: So if they tell you, ‘Behold, He is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or ‘Behold, in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
units.Matthew 24:27: For just as lightning comes from the east and shines to the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
units.Matthew 24:28: Wherever the corpse is, there the eagles will gather.
units.Matthew 24:29: Immediately after the affliction of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its brightness, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
units.Matthew 24:30: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn; they will see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
units.Matthew 24:31: He will send His angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather His chosen from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
units.Mark 13:1: As He was leaving the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, “Teacher, look! What stones and what buildings!”
units.Mark 13:2: Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be torn down.”
units.Mark 13:3: As He sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned Him privately:
units.Mark 13:4: “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be fulfilled?”
units.Mark 13:14: When you see the abomination of desolation standing where it must not—let the reader understand—then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
units.Mark 13:15: Let the one on the housetop not go down or enter to take anything from his house,
units.Mark 13:16: and let the one in the field not turn back to take his garment.
units.Mark 13:17: Woe to those who are pregnant and those nursing infants in those days!
units.Mark 13:18: Pray that it does not happen in winter.
units.Mark 13:19: For those days will be distress such as has not occurred from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and certainly will not occur again.
units.Mark 13:20: If the Lord had not shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen, whom He chose, He shortened the days.
units.Mark 13:21: Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ do not believe it.
units.Mark 13:22: For false christs and false prophets will arise and give signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.
units.Mark 13:23: But you, watch out! I have told you everything beforehand.
units.Mark 13:24: But in those days, after that distress, the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light.
units.Mark 13:25: The stars will be falling from heaven, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
units.Mark 13:26: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
units.Mark 13:27: Then He will send the angels and gather His chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
units.Zechariah 1:1: In the eighth month of the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, Berechiah’s son, son of Addo, the prophet, saying:
units.Zechariah 1:2: “The Lord was angry with your fathers with great anger.
units.Zechariah 1:3: You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Return to Me, and I will return to you, says the Lord.
units.Zechariah 1:4: Do not become like your fathers, against whom the former prophets brought charges, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn away from your evil ways and your evil practices.’ But they did not listen attentively to Me, says the Lord.
units.Zechariah 1:5: Your fathers—where are they? And the prophets—surely they will not live forever?
units.Zechariah 1:6: Yet receive My words and My ordinances, all that I, in My Spirit, command My servants the prophets, who overtook your fathers.” And they answered and said, “As the Lord Almighty has arrayed Himself to act according to your ways and practices, so He acted toward you.”
units.Zechariah 6:1: I turned and lifted my eyes and saw: look, four chariots coming out from between two mountains! The mountains were bronze mountains.
units.Zechariah 6:2: The first chariot had flame-red horses, and the second chariot black horses,
units.Zechariah 6:3: the third chariot white horses, and the fourth chariot dappled, gray horses.
units.Zechariah 6:4: I answered and said to the angel speaking within me, “What are these, lord?”
units.Zechariah 6:5: The angel speaking within me answered, “These are the four winds of heaven; they go out to stand beside the Lord of all the earth.
units.Zechariah 6:6: The one with the black horses was going out toward the northern land; the white ones were going out behind them, and the dappled ones were going out toward the southern land,
units.Zechariah 6:7: and the gray ones were going out and looking to go and travel around the earth.” He said, “Go and travel around the earth!” And they traveled around the earth.
units.Zechariah 6:8: He cried out and said to me, “Look, those going out toward the northern land have brought My wrath to rest in the northern land.”
units.Ezekiel 1:1: And it happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, while I was among the captives by the River Chebar: the heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.
units.Ezekiel 1:2: On the fifth of the month—this was the fifth year of King Jehoiakim’s captivity—
units.Ezekiel 1:3: the Lord’s word came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the River Chebar; and the Lord’s hand came upon me,
units.Ezekiel 1:26: Like the appearance of a sapphire stone was the likeness of a throne upon it; and above the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the form of a human being.
units.Ezekiel 1:27: I saw something like the sight of electrum from the appearance of a waist upward; and from the appearance of a waist down below I saw something like the appearance of fire, with its brightness all around.
units.Ezekiel 1:28: Like the appearance of a bow when it is in the cloud on a rainy day, so was the arrangement of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the Lord’s glory. I saw it, and I fall upon my face, and I heard the voice of One speaking.
units.Ezekiel 2:1: He said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak to you.”
units.Ezekiel 2:2: A spirit came upon me, took me up, raised me, and set me on my feet; I heard Him speaking to me,
units.Ezekiel 2:3: and He said to me, “Son of man, I am sending you out to the house of Israel, those who embitter Me, who have embittered Me, they and their fathers, until this present day,
units.Ezekiel 2:4: and you will say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord.’
units.Ezekiel 3:22: The Lord’s hand came upon me, and He said to me, “Rise and go out to the plain, and you will be spoken to there.”
units.Ezekiel 3:23: I rose and went out to the plain, and behold, the Lord’s glory stood there, like the vision and like the glory I had seen by the River Chebar; and I fall upon my face.
units.Ezekiel 3:24: A spirit came upon me and set me on my feet. He spoke to me and said to me, “Go, be shut inside your house.
units.Ezekiel 3:25: And you, son of man, behold, bonds have been placed upon you, and they will bind you with them; you certainly will not go out from among them.
units.Ezekiel 3:26: I will bind your tongue, and you will become mute; you will not be a man rebuking them, for it is an embittering house.
units.Ezekiel 3:27: But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Let the one who hears hear, and let the one who disobeys disobey,’ for it is an embittering house.”
units.1 Kings 22:19: Micaiah said, “Not so—not I! Hear the Lord’s word—not so! I saw the Lord, the God of Israel, sitting on His throne, and all the army of heaven stood around Him, on His right and His left.
units.1 Kings 22:20: The Lord said, ‘Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Remmath-gilead?’ One said this, and another said that.
units.1 Kings 22:21: A spirit came forward, stood before the Lord, and said, ‘I will deceive him.’ The Lord said to it, ‘By what means?’
units.1 Kings 22:22: It said, ‘I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ He said, ‘You will deceive him and indeed prevail. Go out and do so.’
units.1 Kings 22:23: Now behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken calamities against you.”
units.Matthew 13:36: Then He left the crowds and entered the house. His disciples came to Him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the darnel in the field.”
units.Matthew 13:37: He answered, “The One sowing the good seed is the Son of Man.
units.Matthew 13:38: The field is the world; the good seed are the sons of the kingdom; the darnel are the sons of the evil one;
units.Matthew 13:39: the enemy who sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the consummation of the age; and the reapers are angels.
units.Matthew 13:40: Just as the darnel is gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the consummation of the age.
units.Matthew 13:41: The Son of Man will send His angels, and they will gather from His kingdom all causes of stumbling and those who practice lawlessness.
units.Matthew 13:42: They will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
units.Matthew 13:43: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Let the one who has ears hear.
units.Luke 1:26: In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth,
units.Luke 1:27: to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
units.Luke 1:28: And he entered and said to her, “Rejoice, you who have been favoured! The Lord is with you.”
units.Luke 1:29: She was greatly troubled at the saying and considered what sort of greeting this might be.
units.Luke 1:30: The angel said to her, “Do not fear, Mary, for you have found grace with God.
units.Luke 1:31: And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a Son, and you shall name Him Jesus.
units.Luke 1:32: He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David,
units.Luke 1:33: and He will reign over Jacob’s house forever, and His kingdom will have no end.”
units.Luke 12:22: And He said to His disciples, “For this reason I tell you: do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
units.Luke 12:23: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
units.Luke 12:24: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, and they have neither storeroom nor storehouse, yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!
units.Luke 12:25: And which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his span of life?
units.Luke 12:26: So if you cannot do even the smallest thing, why are you anxious about the rest?
units.Luke 12:27: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They neither toil nor spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
units.Luke 12:28: But if God so clothes the grass that is in the field today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will He clothe you, you of little faith!
units.Luke 12:29: And do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be unsettled,
units.Luke 12:30: for the nations of the world seek after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
units.Luke 12:31: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added to you.
units.Luke 12:32: Do not fear, little flock, because your Father was pleased to give you the kingdom.
units.1 Corinthians 1:1: Paul, called as an apostle of Christ Jesus through God’s will, and Sosthenes the brother,
units.1 Corinthians 1:2: to the Church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called as saints, together with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, theirs and ours:
units.1 Corinthians 1:3: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
units.1 Corinthians 6:1: Does any of you, having a case against another, dare to seek judgment before the unrighteous and not before the saints?
units.1 Corinthians 6:2: Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy of the smallest cases?
units.1 Corinthians 6:3: Do you not know that we will judge angels, to say nothing of matters of ordinary life?
units.2 Thessalonians 1:1: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
units.2 Thessalonians 1:2: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
units.2 Thessalonians 2:1: Now we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to Him,
units.2 Thessalonians 2:2: not to be quickly shaken from your understanding or alarmed, either by a spirit or by a word or by a letter as though from us, as if the day of the Lord is already present.
units.2 Thessalonians 2:3: Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,
units.2 Thessalonians 2:4: who opposes and exalts himself above everything called god or an object of worship, so that he takes his seat in God’s sanctuary, displaying himself as being God.
units.2 Thessalonians 2:5: Do you not remember that when I was still with you I used to tell you these things?
units.2 Thessalonians 2:6: And now you know what restrains, so that he may be revealed in his own time.
units.2 Thessalonians 2:7: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work. Only, the one who now restrains does so until he is out of the way.
units.2 Thessalonians 2:8: And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of His mouth and bring to nothing by the manifestation of His coming.
units.2 Thessalonians 2:9: His coming is according to the working of Satan, with all power and signs and wonders of falsehood,
units.2 Thessalonians 2:10: and with every deception of unrighteousness for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so that they might be saved.
units.2 Thessalonians 2:11: And for this reason God sends them a working of delusion, so that they believe the falsehood,
units.2 Thessalonians 2:12: in order that all who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness may be judged.
units.Luke 2:15: When the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Let us go over to Bethlehem and see this event that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
units.Luke 2:16: They came in haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.
units.Luke 2:17: When they saw Him, they made known the saying spoken to them about this Child.
units.Luke 2:18: Everyone who heard wondered at what the shepherds told them.
units.Luke 2:19: But Mary kept all these matters, pondering them in her heart.
units.Daniel 2:19: Then, in a vision that very night, the king’s mystery was plainly revealed to Daniel. Daniel blessed the Lord Most High,
units.Daniel 2:20: and cried out, “The name of the great Lord will be blessed for ever, because wisdom and majesty belong to Him.
units.Daniel 2:21: He changes seasons and times, transfers kings and appoints them, gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those who possess knowledge,
units.Daniel 2:22: reveals deep and dark things, knows what is in darkness and what is in light, and with Him is a dwelling.
units.Daniel 2:23: To Thee, Lord of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because Thou hast given me wisdom and prudence. Now Thou hast shown me everything I requested, to disclose these things to the king.”
units.Genesis 37:1: And Jacob lived in the land where his father had lived as a stranger, in the land of Canaan.
units.Genesis 37:2: And these are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was tending the sheep with his brothers, a youth among the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives; and Joseph brought an evil report to Israel their father.
units.Genesis 37:3: And Jacob loved Joseph more than all his sons, for he was to him a son of his old age; and he made him a tunic of many colours.
units.Genesis 37:4: And his brothers saw that their father loved him above all his sons, and hated him, and could speak nothing peaceable to him.
units.Genesis 37:5: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and told it to his brothers.
units.Genesis 37:6: And he said to them, “Hear this dream which I have dreamed.
units.Genesis 37:7: “I dreamed that we were binding sheaves in the midst of the plain; and my sheaf arose and stood upright, and your sheaves turned about and bowed down to my sheaf.”
units.Genesis 37:8: And his brothers said to him, “Shall you indeed reign over us, or shall you indeed have dominion over us?” And they hated him still more because of his dreams and because of his words.
units.Genesis 37:9: And he saw another dream, and told it to his father and to his brothers, and said, “Behold, I have dreamed another dream, as though the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”
units.Genesis 37:10: And his father rebuked him, and said to him, “What is this dream which you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow down to you to the earth?”
units.Genesis 37:11: And his brothers envied him, but his father kept the saying in mind.
units.Mark 14:53: They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes assembled.
units.Mark 14:54: Peter followed Him from a distance, as far as inside the high priest’s courtyard. He sat with the attendants and warmed himself at the firelight.
units.Mark 14:55: The chief priests and the whole council sought testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but found none.
units.Mark 14:56: For many bore false witness against Him, but their testimonies did not agree.
units.Mark 14:57: Some stood up and bore false witness against Him, saying,
units.Mark 14:58: “We heard Him say, ‘I will tear down this sanctuary made by hands, and in three days I will build another not made by hands.’”
units.Mark 14:59: Yet even in this their testimony did not agree.
units.Mark 14:60: The high priest stood up in the midst and questioned Jesus, saying, “Dost Thou answer nothing? What is it these men testify against Thee?”

units.Luke 1:5: In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah. He had a wife from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
units.Luke 1:6: Both were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the Lord’s commandments and ordinances.
units.Luke 1:7: They had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in years.
units.Luke 1:8: While he was serving as priest before God in the order of his division,
units.Luke 1:9: according to the priesthood’s custom, he was chosen by lot to enter the Lord’s sanctuary and burn incense.
units.Luke 1:10: The whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of incense.
units.Luke 1:11: An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right of the altar of incense.
units.Luke 1:12: Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
units.Luke 1:13: But the angel said to him, “Do not fear, Zechariah, for your petition has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John.
units.Luke 1:14: You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth,

units.Luke 1:16: He will turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.

units.Luke 1:18: Zechariah said to the angel, “How will I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in years.”
units.Luke 1:19: The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands before God, and I was sent to speak to you and announce this good news to you.
units.Luke 1:20: And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their appointed time.”
units.Luke 1:21: The people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering at his delay in the sanctuary.
units.Luke 1:22: When he came out, he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary. He kept making signs to them and remained mute.
units.Luke 1:23: When the days of his service were completed, he went home.

units.Jeremiah 36:1: And these are the words of the document Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the elders of the deportation, the priests, and the false prophets—a letter to Babylon for the deportees and all the people—

units.Luke 22:8: And He sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat.”

units.Luke 22:10: He said to them, “Behold, as you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters.
units.Luke 22:11: And you shall say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the lodging room in which I may eat the Passover with My disciples?”’
units.Luke 22:12: And he will show you a large, furnished upper room. Prepare it there.”
units.Luke 22:13: They went and found things just as He had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
units.Luke 22:14: When the hour came, He reclined at table, and the apostles with Him.
units.Luke 22:15: And He said to them, “With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
units.Luke 22:16: For I tell you that I will certainly not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
units.1 Kings 8:22: Solomon stood before the Lord’s altar in the presence of the whole assembly of Israel and spread his hands toward heaven.
units.1 Kings 8:23: He said, “Lord, the God of Israel, there is no God like Thee in heaven above or on earth beneath, keeping covenant and mercy with Thy servant who walks before Thee with all his heart,
units.1 Kings 8:24: which Thou keptest for Thy servant David my father; Thou spakest with Thy mouth and didst fulfill it with Thy hands, as it is this day.
units.1 Kings 8:25: Now, Lord, the God of Israel, keep for Thy servant David my father what Thou didst promise him: ‘A man of yours shall not be removed from before Me sitting on Israel’s throne, if only your children guard their ways, walking before Me as you have walked before Me.’
units.1 Kings 8:46: “When they sin against Thee—for there is no person who will not sin—and Thou bringest trouble upon them and givest them over before enemies, and their captors carry them away to a land far and near,
units.1 Kings 8:47: and they turn their hearts in the land where they were deported, return, and plead with Thee in the land of their exile, saying, ‘We have sinned, acted lawlessly, and done wrong,’
units.1 Kings 8:48: and they return to Thee with all their heart and all their soul in the land of their enemies, where Thou didst deport them, and pray to Thee toward their land, which Thou gavest their fathers, the city Thou didst choose, and the house I have built for Thy name,
units.1 Kings 8:49: then hear from heaven, from Thy prepared dwelling place,
units.1 Kings 8:50: and be merciful concerning their wrongs by which they sinned against Thee, and all their acts of faithlessness by which they were faithless to Thee. Grant them compassion before those who took them captive, so that their captors may have compassion on them,
units.1 Kings 8:51: for they are Thy people and Thine inheritance, whom Thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron-smelting furnace.
units.1 Kings 8:52: May Thine eyes and ears be open to Thy servant’s supplication and the supplication of Thy people Israel, to hear them in everything for which they call upon Thee,
units.1 Kings 8:53: for Thou didst set them apart for Thyself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, as Thou spakest through Thy servant Moses when Thou broughtest our fathers out of the land of Egypt, Lord, Lord.”
units.Ezra 7:1: After these events, in the reign of Arthasastha king of the Persians, Esdras went up, son of Saraias, son of Azarias, son of Elkia,
units.Ezra 7:2: son of Saloum, son of Saddouk, son of Achitob,
units.Ezra 7:3: son of Samaria, son of Esria, son of Mareroth,
units.Ezra 7:4: son of Zaraia, son of Saouia, son of Bokki,
units.Ezra 7:5: son of Abisoue, son of Phinees, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the first priest—
units.Ezra 7:6: this Esdras came up from Babylon. He was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the Lord, God of Israel, had given. The king granted him his requests, because the hand of the Lord his God was upon him in everything he sought.
units.Ezra 9:1: When these things were completed, the leaders approached me and said, “The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands in their repulsive practices: the Chanani, Ethi, Pherezi, Iebousi, Ammoni, Moabi, Moseri and Amori,
units.Ezra 9:2: because they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and their sons, and the holy seed has been led astray among the peoples of the lands. The leaders’ hand has been foremost in this covenant-breaking.”
units.Ezra 9:3: When I heard this word, I tore my garments, shook with agitation, plucked hair from my head and beard, and sat quietly.
units.Ezra 9:4: Everyone who pursued the word of the God of Israel gathered to me because of the deported community’s covenant-breaking, while I sat quietly until the evening sacrifice.
units.Ezra 9:5: At the evening sacrifice I rose from my humiliation. As I tore my garments, I shook with agitation; I bend upon my knees and stretch out my hands toward the Lord God,
units.Ezra 9:6: and said, “Lord, I am ashamed and abashed to lift my face toward Thee, for our lawless deeds have multiplied above our heads and our offenses have grown to heaven.
units.Ezra 9:7: From the days of our fathers until this day we have been in great offense. In our lawless deeds, we, our kings and our sons have been handed over into the hand of the kings of the nations—to the sword, captivity, plunder and shame of our face—as on this day.
units.Ezra 9:8: Now the Lord our God has shown us leniency, leaving some of us for deliverance and giving us a support in the place of His sanctuary, to enlighten our eyes and give us a little revival in our slavery.
units.Ezra 9:9: For we are slaves, and in our slavery the Lord our God has not abandoned us. He has inclined mercy toward us before the kings of the Persians, to give us revival, for them to raise up the house of our God and restore its desolate places, and to give us a fence in Judah and Jerusalem.
units.Ezra 9:10: What can we say, our God, after this? For we have abandoned Thy commandments,
units.Ezra 9:11: which Thou gavest us through Thy servants the prophets, saying, ‘The land you are entering to inherit is a land being moved amid the movement of the peoples of the nations, in their repulsive practices, with which they have filled it from mouth to mouth in their uncleanness.
units.Ezra 9:12: Now do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take some of their daughters for your sons. You shall never seek their peace or good, so that you may become strong, eat the good things of the land and bequeath it to your sons for ever.’
units.Ezra 9:13: After everything that has come upon us through our evil deeds and our great offense—for there is none like our God, because Thou hast lightened our lawless deeds and given us deliverance—
units.Ezra 9:14: for we have returned to scattering Thy commandments and intermarrying with the peoples of the lands. Do not be provoked against us to the point of destruction, so that no remnant or survivor remains.
units.Ezra 9:15: Lord, God of Israel, Thou art righteous, for we have been left as survivors, as on this day. Here we are before Thee in our offenses, for because of this there is no standing before Thee.”
units.Psalms 129:1: A song of the ascents. From the depths I have cried unto Thee, Lord.
units.Psalms 129:2: Lord, hear my voice; let Thine ears be attentive to the voice of my petition.
units.Psalms 129:3: If Thou dost closely watch lawless deeds, Lord, Lord, who will withstand?
units.Psalms 129:5: Because of Thy law I waited for Thee, Lord; my soul waited for Thy word.
units.Psalms 129:6: My soul hoped in the Lord from the morning watch until night; from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord.
units.Psalms 129:7: For with the Lord is mercy, and with Him is abundant redemption,
units.Psalms 129:8: And He will redeem Israel from all its lawless deeds.
units.Leviticus 26:14: But if you do not obey Me and do not do these ordinances of Mine,
units.Leviticus 26:15: but disobey them, and your soul is indignant at My judgments, so that you do not do all My commandments, so as to dissolve My covenant,
units.Leviticus 26:16: then I will do this to you: I will bring distress upon you, scab and jaundice that waste your eyes and melt away your life. You shall sow your seeds in vain, and your adversaries shall eat them.
units.Leviticus 26:17: And I will set My face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies. Those who hate you shall pursue you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
units.Leviticus 26:18: And if up to this point you do not obey Me, I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.
units.Leviticus 26:40: And they shall confess their sins and their fathers’ sins, because they transgressed and disregarded Me, and because they walked crookedly before Me.
units.Leviticus 26:41: And I too walked with them in contrary anger, and I will destroy them in their enemies’ land. Then their uncircumcised heart will feel shame, and then they will accept their sins.
units.Leviticus 26:42: And I will remember the covenant of Jacob and the covenant of Isaac, and the covenant of Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.
units.Leviticus 26:43: And the land shall be abandoned by them. Then the land shall receive its Sabbaths when it is desolated because of them, and they shall accept their lawless deeds, because they disregarded My judgments and were indignant at My ordinances in their soul.
units.Leviticus 26:44: And yet even so, while they were in their enemies’ land, I did not disregard them or become indignant with them so as to consume them and dissolve My covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.
units.Leviticus 26:45: And I will remember for them the former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery, before the nations to be their God. I am the Lord.
units.Deuteronomy 29:18: And it shall be, if he hears the words of this curse and pronounces a blessing in his heart, saying, May it be well with me, though I walk in the wandering of my heart—so that the sinner may not destroy the guiltless with him—
units.Deuteronomy 29:19: God will in no wise be willing to be merciful unto him; but then the anger of the Lord and His jealousy shall blaze against that man, and all the curses of this covenant which are written in this book of the law shall cleave unto him, and the Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven.
units.Deuteronomy 29:20: And the Lord shall set him apart for evils from all the sons of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant which are written in this book of the law.
units.Deuteronomy 29:21: And the generation to come, your sons who shall arise after you, and the foreigner who shall come from a far land, shall speak; and they shall see the plagues of that land and its diseases, which the Lord has sent upon it—
units.Deuteronomy 29:22: sulfur and salt, burned over; all its land shall neither be sown nor sprout, neither shall any green thing grow upon it, as at the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew in wrath and anger—
units.Deuteronomy 29:23: and all the nations shall say, Why has the Lord done thus unto this land? What does this great heat of anger mean?
units.Deuteronomy 29:24: And they shall say, Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which He made with their fathers when He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt;
units.Deuteronomy 29:25: and they went and served other gods, and bowed down unto them, whom they did not know, and whom He had not allotted unto them.
units.Deuteronomy 29:26: And the Lord was kindled in wrath against that land, to bring upon it all the curses which are written in this book of the law.
units.Deuteronomy 29:27: And the Lord removed them from their land in wrath, and anger, and exceeding great indignation, and cast them into another land, as it is now.
units.Deuteronomy 29:28: The hidden things belong unto the Lord our God; but the things revealed belong unto us and unto our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.
units.Jeremiah 51:1: The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans living in Egypt’s land and those staying at Migdol, Taphnas, and in Pathoures’s land:
units.Jeremiah 51:2: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: You have seen all the calamities I brought upon Jerusalem and Judah’s cities. Behold, they are deserted of inhabitants,
units.Jeremiah 51:3: because of the wickedness they committed to embitter Me, going to burn incense to other gods whom you did not know.
units.Jeremiah 51:4: I sent you My servants the prophets at dawn, and I sent them saying, Do not commit this act of defilement that I hate.
units.Jeremiah 51:5: But they did not listen to Me or incline their ear to turn from their evils and stop burning incense to other gods.
units.Jeremiah 51:6: My anger and wrath dripped out and blazed in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, and they became a desolation and an untrodden place, as on this day.
units.Jeremiah 51:7: Now thus said the Lord Almighty: Why are you doing great evils against yourselves, cutting off from yourselves man and woman, little child and nursing infant from Judah, so that none of you remains,
units.Jeremiah 51:8: embittering Me with the work of your hands by burning incense to other gods in Egypt’s land, which you entered to live there, so that you are cut off and become a curse and a reproach among all the earth’s nations?
units.Jeremiah 51:9: Have you forgotten your fathers’ evils, the evils of Judah’s kings, your rulers’ evils, and your wives’ evils, which they committed in Judah’s land and outside Jerusalem?
units.Jeremiah 51:10: They have not stopped to this day and have not held fast to My ordinances, which I set before their fathers.
units.Exodus 6:1: And the Lord said to Moses, “Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh; for with a mighty hand he shall let them go, and with an uplifted arm he shall drive them out of his land.”
units.Exodus 6:2: God spoke to Moses and said to him, “I am the Lord.
units.Exodus 6:3: I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as their God, but I did not reveal My name Lord to them.
units.Exodus 6:4: I established My covenant with them, to give them the land of the Canaanites, the land where they sojourned and lived as foreigners.
units.Exodus 6:5: I have heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians enslave, and I have remembered your covenant.
units.Exodus 6:6: Go, say to the sons of Israel: ‘I am the Lord. I will bring you out from the Egyptians’ domination and deliver you from slavery. I will ransom you with an uplifted arm and with great judgment.
units.Exodus 6:7: And I will take you to Myself for a people, and I will be your God; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the oppression of the Egyptians.
units.Exodus 6:8: I will bring you into the land concerning which I stretched out My hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you as an inheritance. I am the Lord.’”
units.Psalms 78:1: A psalm for Asaph. God, nations entered Thine inheritance; they defiled Thy holy temple; they made Jerusalem into a fruit-watchman’s hut.
units.Psalms 78:2: They made the dead bodies of Thy servants food for the birds of heaven, the flesh of Thy holy ones for the beasts of the earth.
units.Psalms 78:3: They poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
units.Psalms 78:4: We became a reproach to our neighbors, sneering and ridicule to those around us.
units.Psalms 78:5: How long, Lord? Wilt Thou be angry to the end? Will Thy jealousy blaze like fire?
units.Psalms 78:6: Pour out Thy wrath upon nations that do not know Thee, and upon kingdoms that did not call on Thy name,
units.Psalms 78:7: for they devoured Jacob and made his place desolate.
units.Psalms 78:8: Do not remember our ancient acts of lawlessness; let Thy compassions swiftly reach us first, for we became very poor.
units.Psalms 78:9: Help us, God our Savior. For the glory of Thy name, Lord, rescue us, and be propitious toward our sins for Thy name’s sake,
units.Psalms 78:10: lest the nations say, “Where is their God?” And let vengeance for the poured-out blood of Thy servants be known among the nations before our eyes.
units.Psalms 78:11: Let the groaning of those in bonds enter before Thee; according to the greatness of Thine arm, preserve the sons of those put to death.
units.Psalms 78:12: Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom their insult with which they insulted Thee, Lord.
units.Psalms 78:13: But we, Thy people and the sheep of Thy pasture, will give Thee thanks for ever; from generation to generation we will proclaim Thy praise.
units.Numbers 6:22: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
units.Numbers 6:23: Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying: Thus you shall bless the sons of Israel, saying unto them (and they shall put My name upon the sons of Israel, and I, the Lord, will bless them):
units.Titus 3:1: Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to obey, and to be ready for every good work,
units.Titus 3:2: to slander no one, to be peaceable, considerate, showing complete gentleness toward all people.
units.Titus 3:3: For we too were once foolish, disobedient, led astray, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, hating one another.
units.Titus 3:4: But when the kindness of God our Savior and His love for humanity appeared,
units.Titus 3:5: He saved us, not on the basis of works done by us in righteousness, but according to His mercy, through the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
units.Titus 3:6: whom He poured out richly upon us through Jesus Christ our Savior,
units.Titus 3:7: so that, justified by His grace, we might become heirs in accordance with the hope of eternal life.
units.Isaiah 65:17: For heaven will be new and earth new, and they will never remember former things, nor will those things enter their heart,
units.Isaiah 65:18: but they will find joy and exultation in it. For behold, I am making Jerusalem an exultation and My people joy.
units.Isaiah 65:19: I will exult over Jerusalem and rejoice over My people, and no sound of weeping or crying will ever again be heard in her.
units.Isaiah 65:20: There will never be one cut off prematurely there, nor an old man who fails to complete his time. For the young person will be a hundred years old, but the sinner who dies will be a hundred years old and accursed.
units.Isaiah 65:21: They will build houses and inhabit them themselves; they will plant vineyards and eat their own produce.
units.Isaiah 65:22: They will not build for others to inhabit or plant for others to eat. For My people’s days will be like those of the tree of life; they will wear out the works of their labor.
units.Isaiah 65:23: My chosen ones will not labor in vain or bear children for a curse, because they are offspring blessed by God, and their descendants will be with them.
units.Isaiah 65:24: Before they cry out I will listen to them; while they are still speaking I will say, ‘What is it?’
units.Isaiah 65:25: Then wolves and lambs will graze together, and a lion will eat straw like an ox, while a serpent will eat earth like bread. They will not wrong or destroy on My holy mountain,” says the Lord.
units.Isaiah 43:22: I did not call you now, Jacob, nor did I make you toil, Israel.
units.Isaiah 43:23: The sheep for your whole burnt offering were not for Me, nor did you glorify Me with your sacrifices, nor did I make you toil with frankincense.
units.Isaiah 43:24: You did not acquire incense for Me with silver, nor did I desire the fat of your sacrifices; instead, amid your sins and wrongdoings I stood over you.
units.Isaiah 43:25: I am, I am the One who wipes out your lawless acts, and I will certainly not remember.
units.Isaiah 43:26: But you, remember, and let us be judged. You, state your lawless acts first, so that you may be justified.
units.Isaiah 43:27: Your first fathers and their rulers acted lawlessly against Me,
units.Isaiah 43:28: and the rulers defiled My holy things, and I gave Jacob over to destruction and Israel to reproach.”
units.Isaiah 44:24: Thus says the Lord who redeems you and forms you from the womb: “I am the Lord who completes all things. I stretched heaven alone and established the earth. Who else
units.Isaiah 44:25: will scatter the signs of spirit-mediums and divinations from the heart, turning the discerning backward and making their counsel foolish,
units.Isaiah 44:26: and establish His servant’s words and make His messengers’ counsel true? He says to Jerusalem, ‘You will be inhabited,’ and to Judea’s cities, ‘You will be rebuilt,’ and her deserted places will spring up;
units.Isaiah 44:27: He says to the abyss, ‘You will be desolate, and I will dry your rivers’;
units.Isaiah 44:28: He tells Cyrus to understand, and says, ‘He will do all My wishes.’ He says to Jerusalem, ‘You will be rebuilt, and I will lay the foundation of My holy house.’”
units.Jeremiah 52:12: In the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuzaradan, the chief guard who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
units.Jeremiah 52:13: He burned the Lord’s house, the king’s house, and all the city’s houses; every great house he burned with fire.
units.Jeremiah 52:14: The Chaldean force with the chief guard pulled down the whole wall of Jerusalem all around.
units.Jeremiah 52:16: The chief guard left the remaining people as vinedressers and farmers.
units.Deuteronomy 1:1: These are the words which Moses spoke unto all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness toward the west, near the Red Sea, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Aulon, and Katachrysea.
units.Deuteronomy 1:2: It is a journey of eleven days from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir unto Kadesh-barnea.
units.Deuteronomy 1:3: And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spoke unto all the sons of Israel, according to all that the Lord had commanded him concerning them.
units.Deuteronomy 1:4: After he had smitten Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who dwelt in Ashtaroth and in Edrei,
units.Deuteronomy 1:5: beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to make this law plain, saying:
units.Joshua 1:1: After the death of Moses, the Lord spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ attendant, saying:
units.Joshua 1:2: “Moses My servant has died. Now therefore arise and cross the Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I am giving them.
units.Joshua 1:3: Every place where you tread with the sole of your feet I will give you, as I have spoken to Moses.
units.Joshua 1:4: The wilderness and Anti-Lebanon, as far as the great river, the River Euphrates, and as far as the furthest sea toward the setting sun shall be your borders.
units.Joshua 1:5: No man shall withstand you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not forsake you or disregard you.
units.Joshua 1:6: Be strong and courageous, for you shall apportion to this people the land which I swore to your fathers to give them.
units.Joshua 1:7: Be strong and courageous, then, to keep and do what Moses My servant commanded you. Do not turn aside from these commands to the right or to the left, so that you may have understanding in all that you do.
units.Joshua 1:8: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth. Meditate on it day and night, so that you may understand how to do all that is written. Then you shall prosper and make your ways prosper, and then you shall understand.
units.Joshua 1:9: Behold, I have commanded you: be strong and courageous. Do not be fainthearted or afraid, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”
units.Acts 9:1: Saul, still breathing threat and murder against the Lord’s disciples, went to the high priest
units.Acts 9:2: and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any belonging to the Way, both men and women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
units.Acts 9:3: As he traveled and drew near Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
units.Acts 9:4: He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?”
units.Acts 9:5: He said, “Who art Thou, Lord?” He answered, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
units.Acts 9:6: But rise and enter the city, and you will be told what you must do.”
units.Acts 9:7: The men traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one.
units.Acts 9:8: Saul rose from the ground, but although his eyes were open, he could see nothing. They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
units.Acts 9:9: For three days he could not see, and he neither ate nor drank.
units.Acts 26:1: Agrippa said to Paul, “You are permitted to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and made his defense:
units.Acts 26:2: “Concerning everything of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to make my defense before you today,
units.Acts 26:3: especially since you are familiar with all the Jewish customs and disputes. Therefore I ask you to hear me patiently.
units.Acts 26:12: In this pursuit I was traveling to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
units.Acts 26:13: when at midday, O king, I saw along the road a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those traveling with me.
units.Acts 26:14: When we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew language: ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against goads.’
units.Acts 26:15: I said, ‘Who art Thou, Lord?’ The Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
units.Acts 26:16: But rise and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and witness of the things in which you have seen Me and those in which I will appear to you,
units.Acts 26:17: rescuing you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you,
units.Acts 26:18: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from Satan’s authority to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an allotted share among those sanctified by faith in Me.’
units.Jude 1:1: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, to those who are called, beloved in God the Father and kept for Jesus Christ:
units.Jude 1:2: May mercy and peace and love be multiplied to you.
units.Jude 1:3: Beloved, while making every effort to write to you about the salvation we share, I found it necessary to write and urge you to contend for the faith delivered once for all to the saints.
units.Jude 1:4: For certain people have slipped in unnoticed, those written about long ago for this judgment: ungodly people who turn the grace of our God into shameless indulgence and deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
units.Jude 1:5: Now I wish to remind you, although you have come to know all this once for all, that Jesus, after saving a people from the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe.
units.Jude 1:6: And He has kept the angels who did not keep their own domain, but abandoned their proper dwelling, in everlasting chains under gloom for the judgment of the great day.
units.Jude 1:7: In the same way, Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, which practiced sexual immorality and went after other flesh in a manner like these, are set before us as an example, undergoing the penalty of eternal fire.
units.Jude 1:8: Yet in the same way these people too, in their dreaming, defile flesh, reject dominion, and slander glorious ones.
units.Jude 1:9: But Michael the archangel, when he was contending with the devil and disputing about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring a slanderous judgment against him, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you.”
units.Jude 1:10: But these people slander whatever they do not know; and what they understand by instinct, like unreasoning animals, becomes the very thing by which they are corrupted.
units.Jeremiah 1:5: Before I formed you in the belly, I know you; before you came out of the womb, I have consecrated you. I have appointed you a prophet to nations.
units.Jeremiah 1:6: I said, O Master Lord! Behold, I do not know how to speak, because I am young.
units.Jeremiah 1:7: The Lord said to me, Do not say, I am young, because you will go to everyone to whom I send you, and you will speak according to everything I command you.
units.Jeremiah 1:8: Do not fear them, because I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord.
units.Jeremiah 1:9: The Lord stretched out His hand toward me and touched my mouth. The Lord said to me, Behold, I have put My words into your mouth.
units.Jeremiah 1:10: Behold, today I have appointed you over nations and kingdoms, to uproot, demolish, destroy, build and plant.
units.Isaiah 6:1: In the year that King Oziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up; and the house was full of His glory.
units.Isaiah 6:2: And seraphim stood around Him: each one had six wings, and each one had six wings; with two they covered their faces, and with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
units.Isaiah 6:3: And one cried to another, saying: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Sabaoth; all the earth is full of His glory.
units.Isaiah 6:4: And the lintel was lifted at the sound of their cry, and the house was filled with smoke.
units.Isaiah 6:5: And I said, Woe is me, for I am pierced to the heart! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips; and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord Sabaoth.

units.Lamentations 1:1: After Israel was taken captive and Jerusalem laid waste, Jeremiah sat weeping and lamented this lament over Jerusalem, saying: How the city once full of peoples sat alone! She has become like a widow, she who was populous among the nations. A ruler among the regions has become subject to tribute.
units.Lamentations 1:2: Weeping, she wept in the night, her tears upon her cheeks. Among all those who love her there is no one to comfort her. All her friends have dealt faithlessly with her; they have become her enemies.
units.Lamentations 1:3: Judea was deported because of her humiliation and her great slavery. She dwelt among the nations; she found no rest. All her pursuers overtook her among those who afflicted her.
units.Lamentations 1:4: Zion’s roads mourn because no one comes at the festival. All her gates are destroyed; her priests groan. Her virgins are led away, and she is embittered within herself.
units.Lamentations 1:5: Those afflicting her have become the head, and her enemies prospered, because the Lord humbled her for her many acts of ungodliness. Her infants went into captivity before the oppressor.
units.Lamentations 1:6: All her beauty has departed from Daughter Zion. Her rulers have become like rams finding no pasture; they went without strength before the pursuer.
units.Lamentations 1:7: Jerusalem remembered the days of her humiliation and rejection, all her desired things from ancient days. When her people fell into the oppressor’s hands and no one helped her, her enemies saw her and laughed at her deportation.
units.Lamentations 1:8: Jerusalem has sinned grievously; therefore she has come into upheaval. All who glorified her humbled her, for they saw her shame. She too groaned and turned backward.
units.Lamentations 1:9: Her uncleanness is at her feet; she did not remember her last things. He brought her down exceedingly; there is no one to comfort her. See, Lord, my humiliation, for the enemy has grown great!
units.Lamentations 1:10: The oppressor spread out his hand over all her desired things. She saw nations enter her sanctuary, those whom Thou didst command not to enter Thine assembly.
units.Lamentations 1:11: All her people groan, seeking bread. They gave her desired things for food to restore life. See, Lord, and behold, for I have become dishonored!
units.Lamentations 1:12: Not to you, all who pass along the road! Turn and see whether there is pain like my pain, which came to be. Speaking against me, the Lord humbled me on the day of His furious anger.
units.Jeremiah 1:11: The Lord’s word came to me, saying, What do you see, Jeremiah? I said, A nut-wood staff.

units.Ezekiel 1:4: and I looked, and behold, a sweeping wind was coming from the north, and a great cloud was within it, with brightness around it and fire flashing like lightning; within it was something like the appearance of electrum, within the fire, and brightness within it.
