units.James 1:10: and the rich person in his humiliation, because he will pass away like a flower of grass.
units.James 1:11: For the sun rose with its scorching heat and dried the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished. So also the rich person will wither in his pursuits.
units.James 1:12: Blessed is the man who endures a trial, because, having been approved, he will receive the crown of life that He promised to those who love Him.
units.1 Thessalonians 1:1: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace.
units.1 Thessalonians 1:2: We always give thanks to God for all of you, mentioning you in our prayers, unceasingly
units.1 Thessalonians 1:3: remembering your work of faith and labor of love and endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ before our God and Father,
units.1 Thessalonians 4:13: But we do not want you to be unaware, brothers, concerning those who are sleeping, so that you may not grieve as the rest do, who have no hope.
units.1 Thessalonians 4:14: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose, so also God, through Jesus, will bring with Him those who have fallen asleep.
units.1 Thessalonians 4:15: For this we say to you by a word of the Lord: we who are alive, who remain until the Lord’s coming, will certainly not precede those who have fallen asleep.
units.1 Thessalonians 4:16: For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a commanding cry, with an archangel’s voice and with God’s trumpet, and the dead in Christ will rise first.
units.1 Thessalonians 4:17: Then we who are alive, who remain, will be caught up together with them in clouds to meet the Lord in the air; and so we will always be with the Lord.
units.1 Thessalonians 4:18: Therefore encourage one another with these words.
units.1 Kings 5:14a: Solomon took Pharaoh’s daughter as his wife and brought her into the City of David until he finished the Lord’s house, his own house, and Jerusalem’s wall.
units.1 Kings 5:14b: Then Pharaoh king of Egypt went up, captured Gezer beforehand, and burned it and the Canaanite who lived in Mergab. Pharaoh gave them as parting gifts to his daughter, Solomon’s wife; and Solomon built Gezer.
units.Luke 22:47: While He was still speaking, behold, a crowd came, and the one called Judas, one of the Twelve, was going before them. He drew near to Jesus to kiss Him.
units.Luke 22:48: But Jesus said to him, “Judas, do you hand over the Son of Man with a kiss?”
units.Luke 22:49: When those around Him saw what was about to happen, they said, “Lord, shall we strike with a sword?”
units.Luke 22:50: And one of them struck the high priest’s slave and took off his right ear.
units.Luke 22:51: But Jesus answered, “Allow this much.” And He touched the ear and healed him.
units.Luke 22:52: And Jesus said to the chief priests and captains of the temple and elders who had come against Him, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
units.Luke 22:53: When I was with you daily in the temple, you did not stretch out your hands against Me. But this is your hour and the authority of darkness.”
units.Nehemiah 9:4: Jesus and the sons of Kadmiel, Sachania son of Sarabia, the sons of Chanani, stood on the Levites’ ascent and cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God.
units.Nehemiah 9:5: The Levites Jesus and Kadmiel said, “Stand up and bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting. They will bless Thy glorious name and exalt it above all blessing and praise.”
units.Luke 13:10: Now He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
units.Luke 13:11: And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of weakness for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up completely.
units.Luke 13:12: When Jesus saw her, He called to her and said, “Woman, you have been released from your weakness.”
units.Luke 13:13: And He laid His hands on her, and at once she was made straight, and she glorified God.
units.Luke 13:14: But the synagogue ruler, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the crowd, “There are six days on which work ought to be done. So come and be healed on those days, and not on the Sabbath day.”
units.Luke 13:15: But the Lord answered him, “Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the manger and lead it away to give it water?
units.Luke 13:16: And this woman, who is a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound for, behold, eighteen years—ought she not to have been released from this bond on the Sabbath day?”
units.Luke 13:17: As He said these things, all who opposed Him were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things being done by Him.
units.Daniel 7:1: In the first year of Baltasar’s reign over the country of Babylonia, Daniel saw a vision at his head upon his bed. Then Daniel wrote the vision he had seen in principal points:
units.Daniel 7:2: “Upon my bed I was watching in dreams by night, and there were four winds of heaven falling upon the great sea.
units.Daniel 7:3: Four beasts came up from the sea, each differing from the other.
units.Daniel 7:4: The first was like a lioness with wings like an eagle’s. I watched until her wings were plucked out, she was lifted from the earth and stood on human feet, and a human heart was given her.
units.Daniel 7:5: After her there was another beast with the likeness of a bear. It stood on one side and had three ribs in its mouth. He spoke in this way: ‘Rise, devour much flesh!’
units.Daniel 7:6: After this I watched another beast, like a leopard. Four wings stretched over it, and the beast had four heads; a tongue was given it.
units.Daniel 7:7: After this I watched in the night vision a fourth beast, fearsome, its terror surpassing in strength. It had great iron teeth, devoured and pounded, trampled all around with its feet, and acted differently from all the beasts before it. It had ten horns,
units.Daniel 7:8: and many plans were in its horns. Another single horn sprouted among them, small among its horns, and three of the earlier horns were withered through it. This horn had eyes like human eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and it made war against the holy ones.
units.Daniel 7:9: I watched until thrones were set in place and an Ancient of Days was seated, wearing a covering like snow, with the hair of His head like pure white wool. The throne was like a flame of fire,
units.Daniel 7:10: and a river of fire came out before Him. A thousand thousands attended Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood beside Him. A court sat, and books were opened.
units.Daniel 7:11: Then I watched the sound of the great words the horn was speaking. The beast was beaten to death, its body perished, and it was given over to burning fire.
units.Daniel 7:12: He removed those around it from their authority, and a span of life was given them for a time and a season.
units.Daniel 7:13: I watched in the night vision, and there, upon the clouds of heaven, one like a son of man was coming. He was present as an Ancient of Days, and those standing by were present with him.
units.Daniel 7:14: Authority was given him, and all the nations of the earth according to their families, and all glory, worshipped him. His authority is everlasting authority that will never be taken away, and his kingdom will never be destroyed.
units.Daniel 7:15: I, Daniel, was disheartened by these things in the night vision,
units.Daniel 7:16: and approached one of those standing there, seeking exact understanding from him concerning all these things. He answered me and explained the judgment of the words:
units.Daniel 7:17: ‘These great beasts are four kingdoms that will perish from the earth.
units.Daniel 7:18: The holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and hold the kingdom for ever, for the age of ages.’
units.Daniel 7:19: Then I wanted exact understanding of the fourth beast, which destroyed everything and was exceedingly fearsome. Its teeth were iron and its claws bronze, devouring everyone all around and trampling with its feet,
units.Daniel 7:20: and of its ten horns upon its head and the single other that sprouted, through which three fell out. That horn had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and its appearance surpassed the others.
units.Daniel 7:21: I observed that horn waging war against the holy ones and routing them,
units.Daniel 7:22: until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the holy ones of the Most High. The time was given, and the holy ones took possession of the kingship.
units.Daniel 7:23: I was told concerning the fourth beast that a fourth kingdom would be upon the earth, surpassing the whole earth, overturning it and grinding it down.
units.Daniel 7:24: As for the kingdom’s ten horns, ten kings will arise, and another king will arise after them. He will surpass the earlier ones in evils and humble three kings.
units.Daniel 7:25: He will speak words against the Most High, wear down the holy ones of the Most High, and expect to alter seasons and law. Everything will be handed into his hands for a time, times, and half a time.
units.Daniel 7:26: The judgment will sit; they will destroy the authority and plan to defile and destroy completely.
units.Daniel 7:27: He gave the kingdom, authority, their greatness, and rule over all the kingdoms under heaven to a holy people of the Most High, to reign with everlasting kingship; all authorities will be subject to him and obey him.
units.Daniel 7:28: Until the account ended, I, Daniel, was greatly overcome with astonishment; my condition changed, and I fixed the matter in my heart.”
units.Daniel 8:1: In the third year of Baltasar’s reign came the vision that I, Daniel, saw after seeing the first one.
units.Daniel 8:2: I saw in the vision of my dream, while I was in the city of Susa in the country of Elymais, still beside the gate of Ailam,
units.Daniel 8:3: that, looking up, I saw a great ram standing opposite the gate. It had horns, one higher than the other, and the higher one was rising.
units.Daniel 8:4: After this I saw the ram charging eastward, northward, westward, and southward. No animals stood before it, and no one rescued from its hands. It did as it wished and was exalted.
units.Daniel 8:5: I was pondering, and a male goat came from the west over the earth’s surface without touching the earth. The goat had a single horn between its eyes.
units.Daniel 8:6: It came against the horned ram that I had seen standing beside the gate and ran at it in furious anger.
units.Daniel 8:7: I saw it approach the ram, become furious with it, strike it, and shatter its two horns. The ram no longer had strength to stand against the goat. It hurled the ram down upon the earth and crushed it, and no one could rescue the ram from the goat.
units.Daniel 8:8: The male goat grew exceedingly strong. When it became strong, its great horn was shattered, and four other horns rose behind it toward the four winds of heaven.
units.Daniel 8:9: From one of them a single strong horn sprouted. It grew strong and struck toward the south, toward the east, and toward the north.
units.Daniel 8:10: It was raised as high as heaven’s stars, but was dashed to the earth from the stars and trampled by them,
units.Daniel 8:11: until the chief commander rescues the captivity. Because of him the ancient mountains were dashed down; their place and sacrifice were removed. He set it down upon the earth, and it prospered and came to pass, and the sanctuary will be made desolate.
units.Daniel 8:12: Sins came upon the sacrifice; righteousness was thrown down to the ground, and he acted and prospered.
units.Daniel 8:13: I heard another holy one speaking, and the other said to the speaking Phelmouni, “How long will the vision stand, and the sacrifice that was removed, and the sin of desolation that was given, and the holy places be made desolate for trampling?”
units.Daniel 8:14: He said to him, “Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days; then the sanctuary will be cleansed.”
units.Daniel 8:15: As I, Daniel, watched the vision, I sought to understand, and there stood opposite me someone with a human appearance.
units.Daniel 8:16: I heard a human voice in the midst of Ulai, calling, “Gabriel, give that one understanding of the vision.” The man cried out and said, “The vision concerns that command.”
units.Daniel 8:17: He came and stood beside where I stood. As he came, I was disturbed and fell upon my face. He said to me, “Understand, son of man, for this vision is still for an appointed hour.”
units.Daniel 8:18: As he spoke with me, I fell asleep face down on the ground. He touched me and raised me on the spot,
units.Daniel 8:19: and said to me, “Behold! I am reporting what will happen at the end of the wrath to the sons of your people; it will still remain until the hours of the appointed time of completion.
units.Daniel 8:20: The ram you saw with the horns is the king of the Medes and Persians.
units.Daniel 8:21: The male goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king himself.
units.Daniel 8:22: As for the four horns that were shattered and rose behind it, four kings of his nation will arise, but not according to his strength.
units.Daniel 8:23: At the end of their kingship, when their sins reach fullness, a king with a shameless face who understands riddles will arise.
units.Daniel 8:24: His strength will be made firm, though not by his own strength. He will destroy astonishingly, prosper, and act; he will destroy rulers and a people of holy ones.
units.Daniel 8:25: His intent will be against the holy ones; falsehood will prosper in his hands, and his heart will be exalted. By deceit he will make many disappear, rise for the destruction of men, make a “gathering of a hand,” and sell.
units.Daniel 8:26: The evening-and-morning vision was found to be true. Now the vision is closed up, for it is still for many days.”
units.Daniel 8:27: I, Daniel, was weak for many days. Then I rose and again conducted royal affairs. I was undone by the vision, and there was no one who understood.
units.Daniel 9:1: In the first year under Darius son of Xerxes, from the Median family who ruled over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
units.Daniel 9:2: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, considered in the books the number of years, when a command came to the land concerning Jeremiah the prophet, to bring Jerusalem’s reproach to its full term: seventy years.
units.Daniel 9:3: I set my face toward the Lord God to find prayer and mercy, with fasts, sackcloth, and ashes.
units.Daniel 9:4: I prayed to the Lord God and confessed, saying, “Behold, Lord, Thou art the great, strong, and fearsome God, keeping the covenant and mercy for those who love Thee and guard Thy commands:
units.Daniel 9:5: we have sinned, done wrong, acted impiously, fallen away, and transgressed Thy commandments and judgments,
units.Daniel 9:6: and have not listened to Thy servants the prophets, to what they spoke in Thy name to our kings, our rulers, our fathers, and every nation upon the earth.
units.Daniel 9:7: Righteousness belongs to Thee, Lord, but shame of face to us as on this day—to the people of Judah, those dwelling in Jerusalem, and all the people Israel, near and far, in all the countries where Thou didst scatter them because of the trespass they committed before Thee.
units.Daniel 9:8: Master, shame of face belongs to us, to our kings, rulers, and fathers, because we have sinned against Thee.
units.Daniel 9:9: To the Lord belong righteousness and mercy, for we have fallen away from Thee
units.Daniel 9:10: and have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to follow Thy law that Thou didst set before Moses and us through Thy servants the prophets.
units.Daniel 9:11: All Israel abandoned Thy law and fell away, refusing to hear Thy voice. The curse and oath written in the law of Moses, God’s servant, came upon us, because we sinned against Him.
units.Daniel 9:12: He established for us His commands, all He spoke against us and against our judges, all Thou didst judge for us, bringing great calamities upon us, such as had not occurred under heaven as occurred in Jerusalem.
units.Daniel 9:13: According to what is written in Moses’ covenant, all the calamities came upon us. Yet we did not seek the face of the Lord our God by departing from our sins and understanding Thy righteousness, Lord.
units.Daniel 9:14: The Lord God kept watch over the calamities and brought them upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in everything He may do, and we did not listen to His voice.
units.Daniel 9:15: Now, Master, Lord our God, who didst bring Thy people out of Egypt with Thine uplifted arm and didst make Thyself a name as on this day: we have sinned and acted in ignorance.
units.Daniel 9:16: Master, according to Thy righteousness, let Thy wrath and anger turn away from Thy city Jerusalem, Thy holy mountain. Because of our sins and our fathers’ acts of ignorance, Jerusalem and Thy people, Lord, are a reproach among all around us.
units.Daniel 9:17: Now, Master, hear Thy servant’s prayer and my supplications. Let Thy face look upon Thy desolate holy mountain, for Thy servants’ sake, Master.
units.Daniel 9:18: Attend with Thine ear, Lord, and hear me. Open Thine eyes and see our desolation and that of Thy city, over which Thy name has been called. For we make our supplication in our prayers before Thee because of Thy mercy, not our righteous deeds.
units.Daniel 9:19: Lord, be propitious! Lord, hear and act, and do not delay, for Thine own sake, Master, because Thy name has been called over Thy city Zion and Thy people Israel.”
units.Daniel 9:20: While I was speaking in prayer, confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and making supplication in prayers before the Lord my God and on behalf of our God’s holy mountain,
units.Daniel 9:21: while I was still speaking in my prayer, the man I had seen at first in my sleep, Gabriel, was carried swiftly and approached me at the hour of the evening sacrifice.
units.Daniel 9:22: He approached and spoke with me, saying, “Daniel, I have just come out to show you understanding.
units.Daniel 9:23: At the beginning of your supplication, a command went out from the Lord, and I came to explain it to you, because you are worthy of pity. Understand the command.
units.Daniel 9:24: Seventy weeks have been determined for your people and the city Zion: for sin to be brought to completion, injustices to become scarce, injustices to be wiped away, the vision to be understood, everlasting righteousness to be given, the vision to be fulfilled, and a holy of holies to be gladdened.
units.Daniel 9:25: You will know, understand, and rejoice. You will find commands to be answered, and you will build Jerusalem as a city for the Lord.
units.Daniel 9:26: After seven and seventy and sixty-two, an anointing will be removed and no longer exist. A kingdom of nations will destroy the city and sanctuary together with the anointed one. Its completion will come with wrath and last until the time of completion; it will be assailed by war.
units.Daniel 9:27: The covenant will prevail for many. It will return again and be rebuilt in breadth and length. At the completion of times, after seven and seventy periods and sixty-two years, until the time of the completion of war, desolation will be removed when the covenant grows strong for many weeks. At the end of the week the sacrifice and libation will be removed. Upon the temple will be an abomination of desolations until completion, and completion will be given upon the desolation.”
units.Daniel 10:1: In the first year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, a command was shown to Daniel, whose name was called Baltasar. The vision and command were true, and the strong multitude will understand the command; I understood it in a vision.
units.Daniel 10:2: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks.
units.Daniel 10:3: I ate no desirable bread; meat and wine did not enter my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until I completed the three weeks of days.
units.Daniel 10:4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was on the bank of the great river, the Tigris,
units.Daniel 10:5: and I lifted my eyes and saw a man clothed in fine linen, with fine linen wrapped around his waist, and light coming from his middle.
units.Daniel 10:6: His body was like a tarshish stone, his face like a flash of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and feet like flashing bronze, and the sound of his speech like the sound of an uproar.
units.Daniel 10:7: I, Daniel, saw this great vision, but the men with me did not see it. Strong fear fell upon them, and they fled in haste.
units.Daniel 10:8: I was left alone and saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; a spirit turned upon me for destruction, and I had no strength.
units.Daniel 10:9: I did not hear the sound of his speech; I had fallen face down upon the earth.
units.Daniel 10:10: He brought a hand toward me and raised me upon my knees, upon the soles of my feet.
units.Daniel 10:11: He said to me, “Daniel, you are a man worthy of pity. Understand the commands I speak to you, and stand in your place, for I have just been sent to you.” As he spoke this command with me, I stood trembling.
units.Daniel 10:12: He said to me, “Do not fear, Daniel. From the first day you set your face to understand and humble yourself before the Lord your God, your word was heard, and I entered because of your word.
units.Daniel 10:13: The general of the king of the Persians stood against me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the foremost rulers, came to help me, and I left him there with the general of the king of the Persians.”
units.Daniel 10:14: He said to me, “I came to show you what will meet your people in the latter days, for the vision is still for days to come.”
units.Daniel 10:15: As he spoke these commands with me, I set my face toward the earth and fell silent.
units.Daniel 10:16: Something like a human hand touched my lips. I opened my mouth, spoke, and said to the one standing opposite me, “My lord, something like a vision turned upon my side, upon me, and there was no strength in me.
units.Daniel 10:17: How can the servant speak with his lord? I have become weak; there is no strength in me, and no breath was left in me.”
units.Daniel 10:18: Again one with a human appearance touched me and strengthened me,
units.Daniel 10:19: and said to me, “You are a man worthy of pity. Do not fear; be well. Take courage and be strong.” As he spoke with me, I became strong and said, “Let my lord speak, for he has strengthened me.”
units.Daniel 10:20: He said to me, “Do you know why I came to you? Now I will return to contend with the general of the king of the Persians. I was going out, and the general of the Greeks was coming in.
units.Daniel 10:21: I will indeed show you the first things in a record of truth. No one was helping with me concerning these except Michael the angel.”
units.Daniel 11:1: In the first year of King Cyrus, he told me to be strong and take courage.
units.Daniel 11:2: “Now I have come to show you the truth. Three kings have stood in opposition in Persia, and the fourth will become richer than all the others. When he grows strong through his wealth, he will rise against every king of the Greeks.
units.Daniel 11:3: A powerful king will arise, exercise great lordship, and do whatever he wishes.
units.Daniel 11:4: When he arises, his kingdom will be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, not according to his might or the lordship with which he ruled. His kingdom will be removed, and he will teach others these things.
units.Daniel 11:5: He will strengthen Egypt’s kingdom, and one of the rulers will overpower him and rule; his rule will be a great rule.
units.Daniel 11:6: At the completion of years he will lead them, and the king of Egypt will enter the northern kingdom to make treaties. He will not prevail, for his arm will not establish strength; his arm and that of those traveling with him will grow numb, and he will remain until the appointed hours.
units.Daniel 11:7: A plant from his root will arise on its own, and the king of the north will come against his force with his strength, cause turmoil, and prevail.
units.Daniel 11:8: He will overthrow their gods together with their cast images, and they will carry their crowds, with their precious vessels, silver, and gold, captive to Egypt. There will be a year for the king of the north.
units.Daniel 11:9: He will enter Egypt’s kingdom for days and return to his land,
units.Daniel 11:10: and so will his son. He will be provoked, gather an assembly of a great crowd, and enter against it, sweeping through. He will pass over, return, and be greatly provoked.
units.Daniel 11:11: The king of Egypt will become angry and fight the king of the north, and the assembled force will be handed into his hands.
units.Daniel 11:12: He will take the assembled force, and his heart will be exalted. He will throw many into turmoil and will not be afraid.
units.Daniel 11:13: The king of the north will return and gather a city’s force larger than the first at the completion of a year’s appointed time. He will enter it against him with a great crowd and much money.
units.Daniel 11:14: In those times designs will rise against the king of Egypt. He will rebuild the fallen things of your nation and arise to establish the prophecy, but they will stumble.
units.Daniel 11:15: The king of the north will come, turn his spears, and take the fortified city. The arms of Egypt’s king will stand with his rulers, but he will have no strength to resist him.
units.Daniel 11:16: The one coming against him will act according to his will, and no one will resist before him. He will stand in the country, and everything will be accomplished in his hands.
units.Daniel 11:17: He will set his face to advance all his undertaking by force and make treaties with him. He will give him a daughter of a human to destroy her, but she will not obey and will not remain.
units.Daniel 11:18: He will set his face toward the sea and take many. He will turn back the wrath of their reproach with an oath according to his reproach.
units.Daniel 11:19: He will turn his face to strengthen his country, but stumble, fall, and not be found.
units.Daniel 11:20: From his root a royal plant will arise, a man striking a king’s glory. In the last days he will be shattered, but not in wrath or war.
units.Daniel 11:21: In his place will arise one easily despised, upon whom royal glory will not be bestowed. He will come suddenly; a king will prevail in his allotment.
units.Daniel 11:22: He will shatter the already-shattered arms before him.
units.Daniel 11:23: With the covenant and a people arrayed with him, he will act falsely and act against a strong nation with a very small nation.
units.Daniel 11:24: He will suddenly desolate a city and do what neither his fathers nor his fathers’ fathers did. He will give them plunder, spoils, and money and devise plans against the strong city, but his plans will be in vain.
units.Daniel 11:25: His strength and heart will be stirred against Egypt’s king with a great crowd. Egypt’s king will be provoked to war with an exceedingly strong crowd, but will not stand, because he will devise a design against him.
units.Daniel 11:26: His anxieties will consume him and turn him away. He will pass through and sweep away, and many wounded will fall.
units.Daniel 11:27: Two kings alone will dine together, eat at one table, and speak falsely, but they will not prosper, for completion still awaits its appointed time.
units.Daniel 11:28: He will return to his country with much money, his heart against the holy covenant. He will act and return to his country
units.Daniel 11:29: at the appointed time. He will enter Egypt, but it will not be as the first and the last.
units.Daniel 11:30: Romans will come, drive him out, and rebuke him. He will return, become angry against the holy covenant, act, and return. He will consider them because they abandoned the holy covenant.
units.Daniel 11:31: Arms from him will arise, defile the sanctuary of fear, remove the sacrifice, and establish an abomination of desolation.
units.Daniel 11:32: In sins against the covenant they will defile with a harsh people, but the people who know these things will be strong and act.
units.Daniel 11:33: The thoughtful of the nation will give understanding to many. They will stumble by the sword and grow old in it; in captivity and plunder they will be stained for days.
units.Daniel 11:34: When they are crushed, they will gather a little strength. Many will assemble with them at a city, and many as in an allotment.
units.Daniel 11:35: Some of those who understand will consider how to purify themselves, be selected, and be cleansed until the time of completion, for the time still awaits its hours.
units.Daniel 11:36: The king will act according to his will, become enraged, and be exalted above every god. He will speak extraordinary things against the God of gods and prosper until the wrath is completed, for completion is coming upon him.
units.Daniel 11:37: He will pay no heed to his fathers’ gods or to the desire of a woman, for he will be exalted in everything, and strong nations will be subject to him.
units.Daniel 11:38: He will stir in his place and honor a god whom his fathers did not know with gold, silver, and costly stone. And with the desirable things
units.Daniel 11:39: of cities he will act, and he will come into a strong fortification. With a foreign god, whom he may acknowledge, he will multiply glory, rule over him greatly, and apportion country as a gift.
units.Daniel 11:40: At the hour of completion, Egypt’s king will clash with him. The king of the north will rage against him with chariots, many horses, and many ships, and enter Egypt’s country
units.Daniel 11:42: and in Egypt’s country no one will be saved.
units.Daniel 11:43: He will control the place of gold, the place of silver, and all Egypt’s desirable wealth; Libyans and Ethiopians will be in his multitude.
units.Daniel 11:44: A report from the east and north will disturb him, and he will go out in strong anger and with a sword to wipe out and kill many.
units.Daniel 11:45: Then he will set his tent between the seas and the mountain of the Holy One’s desire. The hour of his completion will come, and no one will help him.”
units.Daniel 12:1: “At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.
units.Daniel 12:2: Many of those sleeping in the breadth of the earth shall arise: some unto everlasting life, others unto reproach, and others unto dispersion and everlasting shame.
units.Daniel 12:3: Those who understand will appear like heaven’s lights, and those who strengthen my words like the stars of heaven for the age of the age.
units.Daniel 12:4: But you, Daniel, cover the commands and seal the book until the time of completion, until the many go mad and the earth is filled with injustice.”
units.Daniel 12:5: I, Daniel, saw two others standing, one on this side of the river and one on the other.

source_units.text: In the first year of Baltasar’s reign over the country of Babylonia, Daniel saw a vision at his head upon his bed. Then Daniel wrote the vision he had seen in principal points:
“Upon my bed I was watching in dreams by night, and there were four winds of heaven falling upon the great sea.
Four beasts came up from the sea, each differing from the other.
The first was like a lioness with wings like an eagle’s. I watched until her wings were plucked out, she was lifted from the earth and stood on human feet, and a human heart was given her.
After her there was another beast with the likeness of a bear. It stood on one side and had three ribs in its mouth. He spoke in this way: ‘Rise, devour much flesh!’
After this I watched another beast, like a leopard. Four wings stretched over it, and the beast had four heads; a tongue was given it.

After this I watched in the night vision a fourth beast, fearsome, its terror surpassing in strength. It had great iron teeth, devoured and pounded, trampled all around with its feet, and acted differently from all the beasts before it. It had ten horns,

and many plans were in its horns. Another single horn sprouted among them, small among its horns, and three of the earlier horns were withered through it. This horn had eyes like human eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and it made war against the holy ones.
I watched until thrones were set in place and an Ancient of Days was seated, wearing a covering like snow, with the hair of His head like pure white wool. The throne was like a flame of fire,
and a river of fire came out before Him. A thousand thousands attended Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood beside Him. A court sat, and books were opened.
Then I watched the sound of the great words the horn was speaking. The beast was beaten to death, its body perished, and it was given over to burning fire.
He removed those around it from their authority, and a span of life was given them for a time and a season.
I watched in the night vision, and there, upon the clouds of heaven, one like a son of man was coming. He was present as an Ancient of Days, and those standing by were present with him.

Authority was given him, and all the nations of the earth according to their families, and all glory, worshipped him. His authority is everlasting authority that will never be taken away, and his kingdom will never be destroyed.
I, Daniel, was disheartened by these things in the night vision,
and approached one of those standing there, seeking exact understanding from him concerning all these things. He answered me and explained the judgment of the words:
‘These great beasts are four kingdoms that will perish from the earth.
The holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and hold the kingdom for ever, for the age of ages.’

Then I wanted exact understanding of the fourth beast, which destroyed everything and was exceedingly fearsome. Its teeth were iron and its claws bronze, devouring everyone all around and trampling with its feet,
and of its ten horns upon its head and the single other that sprouted, through which three fell out. That horn had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and its appearance surpassed the others.
I observed that horn waging war against the holy ones and routing them,
until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the holy ones of the Most High. The time was given, and the holy ones took possession of the kingship.
I was told concerning the fourth beast that a fourth kingdom would be upon the earth, surpassing the whole earth, overturning it and grinding it down.
As for the kingdom’s ten horns, ten kings will arise, and another king will arise after them. He will surpass the earlier ones in evils and humble three kings.
He will speak words against the Most High, wear down the holy ones of the Most High, and expect to alter seasons and law. Everything will be handed into his hands for a time, times, and half a time.
The judgment will sit; they will destroy the authority and plan to defile and destroy completely.

He gave the kingdom, authority, their greatness, and rule over all the kingdoms under heaven to a holy people of the Most High, to reign with everlasting kingship; all authorities will be subject to him and obey him.
Until the account ended, I, Daniel, was greatly overcome with astonishment; my condition changed, and I fixed the matter in my heart.”
In the third year of Baltasar’s reign came the vision that I, Daniel, saw after seeing the first one.
I saw in the vision of my dream, while I was in the city of Susa in the country of Elymais, still beside the gate of Ailam,
that, looking up, I saw a great ram standing opposite the gate. It had horns, one higher than the other, and the higher one was rising.
After this I saw the ram charging eastward, northward, westward, and southward. No animals stood before it, and no one rescued from its hands. It did as it wished and was exalted.
I was pondering, and a male goat came from the west over the earth’s surface without touching the earth. The goat had a single horn between its eyes.
It came against the horned ram that I had seen standing beside the gate and ran at it in furious anger.

I saw it approach the ram, become furious with it, strike it, and shatter its two horns. The ram no longer had strength to stand against the goat. It hurled the ram down upon the earth and crushed it, and no one could rescue the ram from the goat.
The male goat grew exceedingly strong. When it became strong, its great horn was shattered, and four other horns rose behind it toward the four winds of heaven.
From one of them a single strong horn sprouted. It grew strong and struck toward the south, toward the east, and toward the north.
It was raised as high as heaven’s stars, but was dashed to the earth from the stars and trampled by them,

until the chief commander rescues the captivity. Because of him the ancient mountains were dashed down; their place and sacrifice were removed. He set it down upon the earth, and it prospered and came to pass, and the sanctuary will be made desolate.
Sins came upon the sacrifice; righteousness was thrown down to the ground, and he acted and prospered.

I heard another holy one speaking, and the other said to the speaking Phelmouni, “How long will the vision stand, and the sacrifice that was removed, and the sin of desolation that was given, and the holy places be made desolate for trampling?”
He said to him, “Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days; then the sanctuary will be cleansed.”
As I, Daniel, watched the vision, I sought to understand, and there stood opposite me someone with a human appearance.
I heard a human voice in the midst of Ulai, calling, “Gabriel, give that one understanding of the vision.” The man cried out and said, “The vision concerns that command.”
He came and stood beside where I stood. As he came, I was disturbed and fell upon my face. He said to me, “Understand, son of man, for this vision is still for an appointed hour.”
As he spoke with me, I fell asleep face down on the ground. He touched me and raised me on the spot,
and said to me, “Behold! I am reporting what will happen at the end of the wrath to the sons of your people; it will still remain until the hours of the appointed time of completion.
The ram you saw with the horns is the king of the Medes and Persians.
The male goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king himself.
As for the four horns that were shattered and rose behind it, four kings of his nation will arise, but not according to his strength.
At the end of their kingship, when their sins reach fullness, a king with a shameless face who understands riddles will arise.
His strength will be made firm, though not by his own strength. He will destroy astonishingly, prosper, and act; he will destroy rulers and a people of holy ones.

His intent will be against the holy ones; falsehood will prosper in his hands, and his heart will be exalted. By deceit he will make many disappear, rise for the destruction of men, make a “gathering of a hand,” and sell.
The evening-and-morning vision was found to be true. Now the vision is closed up, for it is still for many days.”
I, Daniel, was weak for many days. Then I rose and again conducted royal affairs. I was undone by the vision, and there was no one who understood.
In the first year under Darius son of Xerxes, from the Median family who ruled over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,

in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, considered in the books the number of years, when a command came to the land concerning Jeremiah the prophet, to bring Jerusalem’s reproach to its full term: seventy years.
I set my face toward the Lord God to find prayer and mercy, with fasts, sackcloth, and ashes.
I prayed to the Lord God and confessed, saying, “Behold, Lord, Thou art the great, strong, and fearsome God, keeping the covenant and mercy for those who love Thee and guard Thy commands:
we have sinned, done wrong, acted impiously, fallen away, and transgressed Thy commandments and judgments,
and have not listened to Thy servants the prophets, to what they spoke in Thy name to our kings, our rulers, our fathers, and every nation upon the earth.

Righteousness belongs to Thee, Lord, but shame of face to us as on this day—to the people of Judah, those dwelling in Jerusalem, and all the people Israel, near and far, in all the countries where Thou didst scatter them because of the trespass they committed before Thee.
Master, shame of face belongs to us, to our kings, rulers, and fathers, because we have sinned against Thee.
To the Lord belong righteousness and mercy, for we have fallen away from Thee
and have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to follow Thy law that Thou didst set before Moses and us through Thy servants the prophets.
All Israel abandoned Thy law and fell away, refusing to hear Thy voice. The curse and oath written in the law of Moses, God’s servant, came upon us, because we sinned against Him.

He established for us His commands, all He spoke against us and against our judges, all Thou didst judge for us, bringing great calamities upon us, such as had not occurred under heaven as occurred in Jerusalem.

According to what is written in Moses’ covenant, all the calamities came upon us. Yet we did not seek the face of the Lord our God by departing from our sins and understanding Thy righteousness, Lord.
The Lord God kept watch over the calamities and brought them upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in everything He may do, and we did not listen to His voice.
Now, Master, Lord our God, who didst bring Thy people out of Egypt with Thine uplifted arm and didst make Thyself a name as on this day: we have sinned and acted in ignorance.

Master, according to Thy righteousness, let Thy wrath and anger turn away from Thy city Jerusalem, Thy holy mountain. Because of our sins and our fathers’ acts of ignorance, Jerusalem and Thy people, Lord, are a reproach among all around us.
Now, Master, hear Thy servant’s prayer and my supplications. Let Thy face look upon Thy desolate holy mountain, for Thy servants’ sake, Master.

Attend with Thine ear, Lord, and hear me. Open Thine eyes and see our desolation and that of Thy city, over which Thy name has been called. For we make our supplication in our prayers before Thee because of Thy mercy, not our righteous deeds.
Lord, be propitious! Lord, hear and act, and do not delay, for Thine own sake, Master, because Thy name has been called over Thy city Zion and Thy people Israel.”
While I was speaking in prayer, confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and making supplication in prayers before the Lord my God and on behalf of our God’s holy mountain,
while I was still speaking in my prayer, the man I had seen at first in my sleep, Gabriel, was carried swiftly and approached me at the hour of the evening sacrifice.
He approached and spoke with me, saying, “Daniel, I have just come out to show you understanding.
At the beginning of your supplication, a command went out from the Lord, and I came to explain it to you, because you are worthy of pity. Understand the command.

Seventy weeks have been determined for your people and the city Zion: for sin to be brought to completion, injustices to become scarce, injustices to be wiped away, the vision to be understood, everlasting righteousness to be given, the vision to be fulfilled, and a holy of holies to be gladdened.
You will know, understand, and rejoice. You will find commands to be answered, and you will build Jerusalem as a city for the Lord.

After seven and seventy and sixty-two, an anointing will be removed and no longer exist. A kingdom of nations will destroy the city and sanctuary together with the anointed one. Its completion will come with wrath and last until the time of completion; it will be assailed by war.

The covenant will prevail for many. It will return again and be rebuilt in breadth and length. At the completion of times, after seven and seventy periods and sixty-two years, until the time of the completion of war, desolation will be removed when the covenant grows strong for many weeks. At the end of the week the sacrifice and libation will be removed. Upon the temple will be an abomination of desolations until completion, and completion will be given upon the desolation.”

In the first year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, a command was shown to Daniel, whose name was called Baltasar. The vision and command were true, and the strong multitude will understand the command; I understood it in a vision.
In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks.
I ate no desirable bread; meat and wine did not enter my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until I completed the three weeks of days.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was on the bank of the great river, the Tigris,
and I lifted my eyes and saw a man clothed in fine linen, with fine linen wrapped around his waist, and light coming from his middle.
His body was like a tarshish stone, his face like a flash of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and feet like flashing bronze, and the sound of his speech like the sound of an uproar.
I, Daniel, saw this great vision, but the men with me did not see it. Strong fear fell upon them, and they fled in haste.
I was left alone and saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; a spirit turned upon me for destruction, and I had no strength.
I did not hear the sound of his speech; I had fallen face down upon the earth.
He brought a hand toward me and raised me upon my knees, upon the soles of my feet.

He said to me, “Daniel, you are a man worthy of pity. Understand the commands I speak to you, and stand in your place, for I have just been sent to you.” As he spoke this command with me, I stood trembling.
He said to me, “Do not fear, Daniel. From the first day you set your face to understand and humble yourself before the Lord your God, your word was heard, and I entered because of your word.

The general of the king of the Persians stood against me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the foremost rulers, came to help me, and I left him there with the general of the king of the Persians.”
He said to me, “I came to show you what will meet your people in the latter days, for the vision is still for days to come.”
As he spoke these commands with me, I set my face toward the earth and fell silent.

Something like a human hand touched my lips. I opened my mouth, spoke, and said to the one standing opposite me, “My lord, something like a vision turned upon my side, upon me, and there was no strength in me.
How can the servant speak with his lord? I have become weak; there is no strength in me, and no breath was left in me.”
Again one with a human appearance touched me and strengthened me,
and said to me, “You are a man worthy of pity. Do not fear; be well. Take courage and be strong.” As he spoke with me, I became strong and said, “Let my lord speak, for he has strengthened me.”
He said to me, “Do you know why I came to you? Now I will return to contend with the general of the king of the Persians. I was going out, and the general of the Greeks was coming in.
I will indeed show you the first things in a record of truth. No one was helping with me concerning these except Michael the angel.”
In the first year of King Cyrus, he told me to be strong and take courage.

“Now I have come to show you the truth. Three kings have stood in opposition in Persia, and the fourth will become richer than all the others. When he grows strong through his wealth, he will rise against every king of the Greeks.
A powerful king will arise, exercise great lordship, and do whatever he wishes.

When he arises, his kingdom will be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, not according to his might or the lordship with which he ruled. His kingdom will be removed, and he will teach others these things.
He will strengthen Egypt’s kingdom, and one of the rulers will overpower him and rule; his rule will be a great rule.

At the completion of years he will lead them, and the king of Egypt will enter the northern kingdom to make treaties. He will not prevail, for his arm will not establish strength; his arm and that of those traveling with him will grow numb, and he will remain until the appointed hours.
A plant from his root will arise on its own, and the king of the north will come against his force with his strength, cause turmoil, and prevail.

He will overthrow their gods together with their cast images, and they will carry their crowds, with their precious vessels, silver, and gold, captive to Egypt. There will be a year for the king of the north.
He will enter Egypt’s kingdom for days and return to his land,
and so will his son. He will be provoked, gather an assembly of a great crowd, and enter against it, sweeping through. He will pass over, return, and be greatly provoked.
The king of Egypt will become angry and fight the king of the north, and the assembled force will be handed into his hands.
He will take the assembled force, and his heart will be exalted. He will throw many into turmoil and will not be afraid.
The king of the north will return and gather a city’s force larger than the first at the completion of a year’s appointed time. He will enter it against him with a great crowd and much money.
In those times designs will rise against the king of Egypt. He will rebuild the fallen things of your nation and arise to establish the prophecy, but they will stumble.
The king of the north will come, turn his spears, and take the fortified city. The arms of Egypt’s king will stand with his rulers, but he will have no strength to resist him.
The one coming against him will act according to his will, and no one will resist before him. He will stand in the country, and everything will be accomplished in his hands.
He will set his face to advance all his undertaking by force and make treaties with him. He will give him a daughter of a human to destroy her, but she will not obey and will not remain.
He will set his face toward the sea and take many. He will turn back the wrath of their reproach with an oath according to his reproach.
He will turn his face to strengthen his country, but stumble, fall, and not be found.
From his root a royal plant will arise, a man striking a king’s glory. In the last days he will be shattered, but not in wrath or war.
In his place will arise one easily despised, upon whom royal glory will not be bestowed. He will come suddenly; a king will prevail in his allotment.
He will shatter the already-shattered arms before him.
With the covenant and a people arrayed with him, he will act falsely and act against a strong nation with a very small nation.

He will suddenly desolate a city and do what neither his fathers nor his fathers’ fathers did. He will give them plunder, spoils, and money and devise plans against the strong city, but his plans will be in vain.

His strength and heart will be stirred against Egypt’s king with a great crowd. Egypt’s king will be provoked to war with an exceedingly strong crowd, but will not stand, because he will devise a design against him.
His anxieties will consume him and turn him away. He will pass through and sweep away, and many wounded will fall.
Two kings alone will dine together, eat at one table, and speak falsely, but they will not prosper, for completion still awaits its appointed time.
He will return to his country with much money, his heart against the holy covenant. He will act and return to his country
at the appointed time. He will enter Egypt, but it will not be as the first and the last.
Romans will come, drive him out, and rebuke him. He will return, become angry against the holy covenant, act, and return. He will consider them because they abandoned the holy covenant.
Arms from him will arise, defile the sanctuary of fear, remove the sacrifice, and establish an abomination of desolation.
In sins against the covenant they will defile with a harsh people, but the people who know these things will be strong and act.
The thoughtful of the nation will give understanding to many. They will stumble by the sword and grow old in it; in captivity and plunder they will be stained for days.
When they are crushed, they will gather a little strength. Many will assemble with them at a city, and many as in an allotment.
Some of those who understand will consider how to purify themselves, be selected, and be cleansed until the time of completion, for the time still awaits its hours.

The king will act according to his will, become enraged, and be exalted above every god. He will speak extraordinary things against the God of gods and prosper until the wrath is completed, for completion is coming upon him.
He will pay no heed to his fathers’ gods or to the desire of a woman, for he will be exalted in everything, and strong nations will be subject to him.
He will stir in his place and honor a god whom his fathers did not know with gold, silver, and costly stone. And with the desirable things
of cities he will act, and he will come into a strong fortification. With a foreign god, whom he may acknowledge, he will multiply glory, rule over him greatly, and apportion country as a gift.
At the hour of completion, Egypt’s king will clash with him. The king of the north will rage against him with chariots, many horses, and many ships, and enter Egypt’s country
and come into my country,
and in Egypt’s country no one will be saved.
He will control the place of gold, the place of silver, and all Egypt’s desirable wealth; Libyans and Ethiopians will be in his multitude.
A report from the east and north will disturb him, and he will go out in strong anger and with a sword to wipe out and kill many.
Then he will set his tent between the seas and the mountain of the Holy One’s desire. The hour of his completion will come, and no one will help him.”

“At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.
Many of those sleeping in the breadth of the earth shall arise: some unto everlasting life, others unto reproach, and others unto dispersion and everlasting shame.
Those who understand will appear like heaven’s lights, and those who strengthen my words like the stars of heaven for the age of the age.
But you, Daniel, cover the commands and seal the book until the time of completion, until the many go mad and the earth is filled with injustice.”
I, Daniel, saw two others standing, one on this side of the river and one on the other.
I said to the one clothed in fine linen above, “When, then, will the wonders you have told me reach completion, and these things be cleansed?”

I heard the one clothed in fine linen above the river’s water say, “Until the time of completion.” He raised his right hand and his left to heaven and swore by God who lives for ever that in a time, times, and half a time would be the completion of the “hands of release” of a holy people, and all these things would be completed.
I heard, but did not understand the time from him. I said, “My lord, what is the interpretation of this word, and what do these figures concern?”
He said to me, “Go away, Daniel, for the commands are covered and sealed until
many are tested and made holy, and sinners sin. None of the sinners will understand, but those who understand will pay attention.
From when the sacrifice is removed for all time and preparations are made to set up the abomination of desolation: one thousand two hundred ninety days.
Blessed is the one who perseveres and reaches a total of one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
But you, go and rest, for there are still days and hours until completion is fulfilled. You will rest and arise unto your glory at the completion of days.”

full_triples.rationale: Daniel's multitude of attendants stand beside the enthroned figure as a court sits. Micaiah sees the heavenly army around the Lord's throne and hears deliberation concerning Ahab. Daniel additionally describes a fiery river and opened books.

target_units.text: Micaiah said, “Not so—not I! Hear the Lord’s word—not so! I saw the Lord, the God of Israel, sitting on His throne, and all the army of heaven stood around Him, on His right and His left.
The Lord said, ‘Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Remmath-gilead?’ One said this, and another said that.
A spirit came forward, stood before the Lord, and said, ‘I will deceive him.’ The Lord said to it, ‘By what means?’
It said, ‘I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ He said, ‘You will deceive him and indeed prevail. Go out and do so.’

The kingdom's permanence is shared, while the source explicitly describes authority being given.

full_triples.rationale: Daniel describes four kings from his nation arising, but not according to his strength. Maccabees describes Alexander dividing his kingdom among officers who take power and wear diadems. The target does not number them as four, and the comparison does not identify each horn or equate the succession details.

target_units.text: He summoned his distinguished officers, who had been brought up with him from his youth, and divided his kingdom among them while he was still alive.
Alexander reigned twelve years, and he died.
His officers took power, each in his own place.
They all put on diadems after his death, and their sons after them for many years; they multiplied evils on the earth.

full_triples.rationale: Daniel sees the vision while his companions do not, becoming frightened and fleeing. The heavenly light flashes around Saul and he hears Jesus, while his companions hear the voice but see no one. The selective perception is comparable, but Acts says the companions stand speechless rather than flee.

target_units.text: As he traveled and drew near Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?”
He said, “Who art Thou, Lord?” He answered, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
But rise and enter the city, and you will be told what you must do.”
The men traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one.

full_triples.rationale: A human-like hand touches Daniel's lips and he opens his mouth to speak. The Lord stretches out His hand and touches Jeremiah's mouth, putting His words there.
